item.title: OpenAI hires former Patreon executives to lead creator product strategy
item.description:
OpenAI hires former Patreon executives to lead creator product strategy

OpenAI announced it is bringing three former Patreon executives onto its creator‑product team. The move gives OpenAI the talent behind the modern creator‑subscription economy.

🔍 Overview

  • OpenAI hired three former Patreon execs to anchor its product strategy for creators.
  • Sam Yam, co‑founder and technology chief of Patreon, will lead Creator Product at OpenAI.
  • Former Patreon product head Drew Rowny and engineering head Shannon Ma have also joined the new venture.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Yam announced his move on X, noting: “We’re going to build together with Creators at OpenAI and share early access to a new set of tools that I think will be critically valuable to Creators and their communities.”
  • He also urged: “Pay attention to OpenAI DevDay next week! I’m becoming active today (and experimenting with some innovative early tools here!)”
  • OpenAI DevDay is scheduled for Tuesday, September 29th, and an Altman post teases another big announcement later in the week.
  • The hiring suggests OpenAI is exploring entry into the creator‑monetization market, building on Patreon’s subscription‑economy blueprint.

📋 Team Table

Person Former Patreon Role
Sam Yam Co‑founder & Technology Chief
Drew Rowny Product Head
Shannon Ma Engineering Head

💡 Why it matters

  • By adding the team that built Patreon’s subscription platform, OpenAI positions itself to offer tools that help creators monetize and grow their communities.
  • Patreon faces a talent loss as Yam departs, shortly after announcing a major feature roadmap and after a January layoff of 20 % of staff.

#OpenAI #Patreon #CreatorEconomy #DevDay

Source: OpenAI nabs key Patreon execs ahead of upcoming announcement

item.title: Google partners with MrBeast for multi-year Gemini and Fitbit promotion
item.description:
Google partners with MrBeast for multi-year Gemini and Fitbit promotion

Google has signed a multi-year partnership with Jimmy “MrBeast” Donaldson, one of YouTube’s biggest creators, to promote Gemini, Google Health, and the Fitbit Air across upcoming videos.

🔍 Overview

The deal marks a significant collaboration between Google and Donaldson, whose YouTube channel became the first to hit 500 million subscribers a couple of months ago. The partnership comes amid reported efforts by YouTube to keep prominent creators exclusive to its platform.

⚙️ Key details

  • Partnership scope: Multi-year agreement featuring Gemini, Google Health, and Fitbit Air
  • First video: Scheduled for September 5
  • Format: Wilderness survival challenge with Jimmy and his crew
  • Additional promotion: Donaldson will appear in a Gemini campaign from Google

🧩 How it works

The inaugural video will follow Donaldson and his crew as they attempt to survive extreme and treacherous climates. Teams will race to navigate three unforgiving landscapes:

  • The jungle
  • The desert
  • The Arctic

According to Google, participants will use Gemini to help them identify dangers, survive brutal weather changes, and stay one step ahead. Donaldson will also use a Fitbit Air in one of his upcoming challenges.

🚀 Availability

Element Detail
First video release September 5
Featured products Gemini, Google Health, Fitbit Air
Campaign type Multi-year partnership with dedicated videos and campaign appearance

💡 Why it matters

The partnership reflects broader platform dynamics in the creator economy. A recent Bloomberg report noted that YouTube has been offering prominent creators deals to keep their content exclusive to its site as more creators strike deals with Netflix.

#MrBeast #GoogleGemini #Fitbit #YouTube #AIpartnerships #creatoreconomy

Source: Google is sending MrBeast into the wilderness, armed with AI
